#!/bin/bash

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --cpus-per-task=24
#flux: -t 12h
#flux: --gpus=1

# The original script requested 2G per CPU core (--mem-per-cpu=2G) for 24 cores.
# This translates to a total of 48G for the single task.
#flux: --mem-per-task=48G

# The following SLURM directive does not have a direct Flux equivalent:
# #SBATCH -J "1RST_fe_complex"
# In Flux, the job name is typically set on the command line, e.g.,
# flux submit -J "1RST_fe_complex" ...

# This script is intended to be run as part of a job array.
# The SLURM directive was: #SBATCH --array=00-19
# To run this with Flux, use bulksubmit, which provides the $FLUX_TASK_ID variable:
# flux mini bulksubmit --tasks=0-19 ./your_script_name.sh

module purge
module load cuda/11.4 gromacs/2021.4

# FLUX_TASK_NCORES corresponds to the value set by --cpus-per-task for a single-task job.
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$FLUX_TASK_NCORES

# FLUX_TASK_ID is the equivalent of SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID for bulk jobs
export COMPLEX=1RST_pep
export TASK_ID=$(printf "%02d" $FLUX_TASK_ID)

mkdir lambda.${TASK_ID}
cd lambda.${TASK_ID}

mkdir ENMIN
cd ENMIN 
gmx grompp -f ../../MDP/ENMIN/enmin.${TASK_ID}.mdp -c ../../$COMPLEX.gro -p ../../$COMPLEX.top -o enmin.tpr
gmx mdrun -v -stepout 1000 -s enmin.tpr -deffnm enmin -ntmpi 1

cd ../
mkdir NVT 
cd NVT
gmx grompp -f ../../MDP/NVT/nvt.${TASK_ID}.mdp -c ../ENMIN/enmin.gro -p ../../$COMPLEX.top -o nvt.tpr -r ../ENMIN/enmin.gro
gmx mdrun -v -stepout 1000 -s nvt.tpr -deffnm nvt -ntmpi 1

cd ../
mkdir NPT
cd NPT
gmx grompp -f ../../MDP/NPT/npt.${TASK_ID}.mdp -c ../NVT/nvt.gro -t ../NVT/nvt.cpt -p ../../$COMPLEX.top  -o npt.tpr -r ../NVT/nvt.gro
gmx mdrun -v -stepout 1000 -s npt.tpr -deffnm npt -ntmpi 1

cd ../
mkdir PROD
cd PROD
gmx grompp -f ../../MDP/PROD/prod.${TASK_ID}.mdp -c ../NPT/npt.gro -t ../NPT/npt.cpt -p ../../$COMPLEX.top  -o prod.tpr -r ../NPT/npt.gro
gmx mdrun -v -stepout 1000 -s prod.tpr -deffnm prod -dhdl dhdl -ntmpi 1

cd ../../

reasons: The resource directive '#flux: --gpus=1' is ambiguous. While it may be accepted by the command line, the canonical and more explicit option for assigning GPUs to tasks within a job specification is '--gpus-per-task=1'.
issues: The 'mkdir' commands will fail if the directories already exist, which could happen if the job is resubmitted after a partial failure. Using 'mkdir -p' is more robust as it does not error if the directory exists.

The script's logic relies heavily on relative paths and changing directories ('cd'). This can be fragile. If any 'cd' command fails, subsequent commands will execute in the wrong directory, leading to errors. Using subshells, e.g., '(cd PROD && gmx grompp ...)', can make the script more resilient.
